title: A Regiment for the Compass
premise: Kestrel Dunmore, a courier carrying the final census codes of the Republic of Vell, arrives in the river town of Ashmoor to deliver documents to a besieged printing workshop. When a sharp-eyed imperial census taker begins asking questions no one should ask, Kestrel realizes their carefully maintained invisibility is a fiction—and that the workshop's printers are compiling a true record of the republic's fall that the new regime will burn at any cost. Torn between loyalty to the courier oath and the truth the census taker offers, Kestrel must choose whose history gets written. In the end, Kestrel smuggles the completed record out as the workshop burns, trading their own name for the survival of everyone else's.
about_author: Juniper Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging confiscated letters in a provincial records office before turning to fiction. They write about ordinary people caught in the machinery of history, and about the paper trails that outlive empires.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Paper
chapters.summary: Kestrel, POV first person, travels by barge toward Ashmoor disguised as a grain clerk, rehearsing their cover story. A flashback establishes the courier oath: carry, never read. The emotional beat is quiet dread beneath practiced blandness—history happens to other people, and Kestrel intends to keep it that way.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: At the town gate, census taker Odile Vane processes arrivals with bureaucratic charm until she asks Kestrel to state their mother's maiden name—a question absent from every prior census. Kestrel lies smoothly but leaves shaken. POV alternates briefly to Odile, revealing she collects discrepancies. Beat: the mask holds, barely.

chapters.title: Ashmoor in Winter Light
chapters.summary: Kestrel scouts the town: occupied streets, ration lines, imperial proclamations pasted over older notices. They locate the print workshop behind a chandler's shop, watching it for a day. Emotional beat: the creeping realization that this sleepy town is already conquered, and Kestrel walked into its last chapter.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: Kestrel makes contact with Master Printer Halvard Brann through a chalked sign only couriers know. Inside, presses run night shifts on something larger than pamphlets. Halvard refuses to explain; Kestrel delivers the codes without reading them. Beat: relief curdling into suspicion—what has Kestrel just enabled?

chapters.title: What the Codes Unlock
chapters.summary: Kestrel learns the codes are decryption keys for sealed archives: testimony, ledgers, names of the disappeared—the republic's true death record. Halvard's press is printing it as a book. Kestrel, furious at being used, nearly walks out. Beat: anger masking fear; the oath says carry, not comprehend.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger of Small Doubts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV: she interviews townsfolk, cross-referencing answers against grain receipts and church rolls. She flags 'the grain clerk' whose hands are ink-stained. Her superiors want compliance, not curiosity, but Odile believes order requires truth—even if her truth serves the empire. Beat: an antagonist who thinks she's the honest one.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Odile summons Kestrel for a follow-up interview, probing gently while a soldier looms. Kestrel survives by volunteering mundane details and letting Odile catch one small lie, satisfying her pattern-hunger. Beat: the thrill and terror of lying well, and the cost of each successful deception.

chapters.title: The Compositor's Daughter
chapters.summary: Kestrel befriends Sela, Halvard's daughter, who sets type by touch in the dark. Through her, Kestrel sees the book taking shape—pages naming people the empire erased. Kestrel reads their own father's name among the testimony. Beat: grief cracking open the belief that history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: A Courier Does Not Read
chapters.summary: Haunted by the name, Kestrel breaks the oath and reads the manuscript overnight. Flashbacks reconstruct their father's arrest and the family myth of neutrality. Kestrel understands now why they were chosen: the archive contains him. Beat: identity collapsing and reforming around a buried truth.

chapters.title: The Informant in the Loft
chapters.summary: Someone has been reporting press activity; a raid narrowly misses the workshop. Suspicion falls on the chandler's apprentice. Kestrel and Sela move the type matrices to a cellar. Beat: paranoia tightening the community; loyalty becomes a matter of life and death.

chapters.title: Odile Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Odile privately reveals she knows what the workshop prints—and offers Kestrel immunity in exchange for the master plates. She argues the record will burn either way, and survival is the only justice available. Beat: the central temptation stated plainly; truth versus loyalty given a face.

chapters.title: Halvard's Confession
chapters.summary: Halvard admits he requested a courier with Kestrel's surname, gambling that blood would bind them to the work. Kestrel rages at the manipulation, then stays anyway—choosing the work over the man. Beat: betrayal transmuted into resolve; Kestrel stops being cargo and becomes author.

chapters.title: Printing by Candlelight
chapters.summary: A montage chapter: the workshop races to finish the print run as garrison patrols thicken. Kestrel learns to set type beside Sela, hands finally matching the story they carry. Beat: hard-won belonging; the quiet joy of craft amid danger.

chapters.title: The Census Closes
chapters.summary: Odile completes the town register and submits her report, including the grain clerk anomaly. Her superior orders the workshop seized and burned as sedition, scheduled in three days. Odile hesitates—her truth was meant to be recorded, not destroyed. Beat: antagonist's crisis of faith.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Kestrel plans the impossible: move four hundred bound copies out under patrol eyes. Routes are mapped, bribes arranged, alibis built. Odile watches Kestrel's window from across the square, undecided. Beat: ticking-clock tension; every ally's courage tested in advance.

chapters.title: The Chandler's Fire
chapters.summary: A diversionary fire set by the suspected informant goes wrong, burning half the chandler's shop and drawing the garrison early. The raid moves up to tomorrow. Someone must hold the soldiers at the door while the books go out. Beat: catastrophe forcing the final choice forward.

chapters.title: What Odile Decides
chapters.summary: Odile, ordered to lead the seizure, instead delays the warrant with a forged clerical error—buying one night, damning her career. She confronts Kestrel: not forgiveness, but a bargain—her testimony added to the book, her name written honestly. Beat: enemy becoming witness; justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: The Long Night of the Press
chapters.summary: The final print run through till dawn: Halvard at the press, Sela composing, Kestrel collating, Odile standing watch. The last page carries the names of everyone who made it—including, at Kestrel's insistence, the informant, forgiven. Beat: exhausted communion; the book becomes the town.

chapters.title: Burning Bright
chapters.summary: Soldiers arrive at sunrise. Halvard refuses to leave and fires the workshop himself rather than surrender it, dying inside as the books leave by river barge hidden under grain sacks. Kestrel watches the smoke from the water. Beat: sacrifice; the workshop stands forever by ceasing to stand.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: At the border checkpoint, Odile—now fugitive—inspects the barge herself and waves it through, erasing Kestrel from the census with her own hand. Kestrel offers her a place on the boat; she chooses to stay and face consequences, her testimony already aboard. Beat: mercy exchanged across enemy lines.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Safe beyond the river, Kestrel writes their real name into the book's colophon—the first time they've claimed it since childhood. Copies are dispersed to sympathetic houses across three provinces, untraceable, unstoppable. Beat: identity reclaimed; invisibility traded for permanence.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What Survives
chapters.summary: Years later, an old archivist catalogs a recovered copy of the Ashmoor Record and finds Kestrel's name beside Halvard's, Sela's, and Odile Vane's. History, it turns out, happened here, to these people—and because they wrote it down, it belongs to everyone. Final beat: the courier's oath fulfilled at last: carried, delivered, read.
